newsitem.title: USA: NASD fines California firm on muni markup charges.
newsitem.headline: NASD fines California firm on muni markup charges.

text.p: NASD said Tuesday it fined First California Capital Markets Inc. in San Francisco and one of its bond salesmen $27,000 for excessive markups in the sale of water district bonds to customers in 1994.

The National Association of Securities Dealers said the firm, which is the subject of a separate SEC muni bond probe, and its salesman Gerald Beldon Porter Jr. agreed to settle charges without admitting or denying the allegations.

At issue are 28 different sales by Porter in September 1994 of four issues of Borrego California Water District Bonds, NASD documents say. The four "distinct" bonds had different maturity dates and interest rates, NASD staff said.
Porter sold most of the bonds at 83 compared to the highest interdealer price of 76.29, for a markup of 6.7 points or 8.79 percent, NASD staff said.
NASD also said that Porter sold the bonds without first being registered with regulators as a municipal securities principal.
NASD documents in the case point to a "continuing uncertainty in the area of municipal securities pricing."
"There is no mark-up guideline for municipal securities. Rather, the cases merely hold that mark-ups on debt securities should generally be lower than for equities," staff documents say.

Separately, the Securities and Exchange Commission has been examining the firm since 1994 in connection with its underwriting of some troubled land based financings by several small Northern California localities.

Reuters reported in August 1995 that SEC sent so-called Wells notices to First Califonia and several other bond professionals as well as some of the localities involved in the deals. The probe is continuing, reliable sources say.
An SEC "Wells" notice tells the recipient that the agency tentatively plans to bring enforcement action against it.
First California attorney Charles Klinedinst, a partner with Hoffman, Finney & Klinedinst in San Francisco, was unavailable for comment.
